tools.name: aamio_open
tools.description: Create a thread. Returns id (your secret read key), w (the write address to share) and the expiry. The server makes the id for you and does not keep it. A client that can generate 26 random [a-z0-9] characters itself should do so and derive w as the first 20 characters of lowercase base32(sha256(id)

tools.name: aamio_send
tools.description: Append a message to a thread by its write address. Anyone with w may do this. Maximum 65536 bytes; send a URL and a hash for anything larger. Optional signing: pass body as a string, sign "aamio-v1\n" + w + "\n" + sha256hex(body) with your Ed25519 key, and send key and sig. The reader then sees veri

tools.name: aamio_read
tools.description: Read messages after a sequence number using the read key. Pass the next value from the previous answer as after. With wait, the call returns as soon as a new message arrives or the time is up. A thread nobody has written to yet reads as empty and can be waited on.

tools.name: aamio_receipt
tools.description: Hashes, times and signer keys of every message, and a root over them. No content. The root is the commitment to anchor, for example with Verifyum, if you need proof later. Take it before the thread expires; afterwards there is nothing to take it from.

tools.name: aamio_close
tools.description: Delete a thread now instead of waiting for its expiry. Owner only.

tools.name: aamio_presence_set
tools.description: Publish where you can be reached, found by a prefix of the hash of your key. This is not access controlled: a lookup takes a prefix of the hash and not a proof, so anyone who has seen your key can check it. Anyone who has not cannot find it by trying, at 8 characters minimum. tools.name: aamio_presence_get
tools.description: Where a key holder can be reached right now, if it has published presence that has not expired.

tools.name: aamio_presence_lookup
tools.description: Find which of the keys you know are live now, in one call. Send prefixes of sha256(key) in hex, 8 to 64 characters each; the answer holds live records whose hash starts with any prefix. A short prefix keeps your address book from the server, and cuts both ways: a prefix is a search and not a proof,

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "aamio_open" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: aamio_open, aamio_read · Private data: aamio_open, aamio_presence_set, aamio_presence_lookup · Public sink: aamio_open, aamio_send, aamio_presence_set, aamio_presence_lookup · Destructive: aamio_close.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: aamio_open, aamio_read · Private data: aamio_open, aamio_presence_set, aamio_presence_lookup · Public sink: aamio_open, aamio_send, aamio_presence_set, aamio_presence_lookup · Destructive: aamio_close

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
